newsitem.title: GERMANY: German politician accuses Turkey of EU blackmail.
newsitem.headline: German politician accuses Turkey of EU blackmail.

text.p: A senior member of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Thursday accused Turkey of "blackmail" by threatening to veto NATO expansion unless it wins closer ties with the European Union.

"Anyone who threatens with a veto even before they're even a member of the EU doesn't make their acceptance any easier," SPD foreign policy spokesman Karsten Voigt told German Radio. "On the contrary, they make it more difficult."
Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller made clear this week Turkey could veto NATO plans to expand into former communist eastern Europe unless the EU delivered on closer ties.
Voigt warned Ciller her threat would be counterproductive, simply alienating Turkey's supporters inside the Union.
"I want a European Union capable of action. We already have enough problems with countries which are always threatening to veto," Voigt said.
"When a country threatens with a veto before it's even a member...then I say Turkey is not yet politically mature enough for Europe," he said.
Ciller met foreign ministers from Britain, France, Germany, Spain and Italy in Rome on Wednesday to discuss relations between Turkey and the EU.
The EU ministers told Ciller Turkey had every right to aspire to full EU membership but must make progress on human rights, the Kurdish issue and its disputes with Greece.
